Articles 214–231 – High Courts
Retirement age – 62 years
Court of Record – Article 215
Writ power – Article 226
Superintendence – Article 227
Transfer – Article 222
Impeachment removal

items: Article 226 (Writ Power) vs Article 32 (Supreme Court Writ Power) is a frequent competitive exam question.
High Court judge retirement age is 62 years (often confused with Supreme Court judge retirement age of 65 years).
Article 215 declares High Courts as Courts of Record with power to punish for contempt.
Article 222 specifically addresses the transfer of High Court judges.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 214 to 231 of the Indian Constitution cover provisions regarding the High Courts.
The retirement age for a High Court judge is 62 years.
High Courts act as a Court of Record under Article 215.
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental and constitutional rights.
Article 227 deals with the High Court's power of superintendence over all subordinate courts.
Article 222 governs the transfer of judges from one High Court to another.
